messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — I'm starting a staged rollout of the ingest JSON schema v2.1 for fleet logs. Goal: smaller payloads, explicit pii hooks, and per-region sampling controls to tame egress and Grafana noise. Specs here: https://rwd-infra/schemas/ingest/v2.1

maria: Do we have a plan for how this affects our existing Prom/Grafana alerts? Last time schema changes spiked the error-rate SLO because alerts parsed fields that moved.

alex: Good call. Plan is: 1) compatibility layer in the parser for 30d, 2) add fallback fields so dashboards don't break, 3) tune alert rules to use stable keys (trace_id, host_id, shard). We'll also annotate dashboards with schema version.

jun: For region constraints — can we make sampling rate configurable per region/cluster? APAC egress is $$$ and GPU capacity is limited in us-east-1 sometimes. I propose default sampling: control-plane=1.0, gpu-prod=0.15, gpu-staging=0.02, edge-regions=0.05. Thoughts?

sam: Agree on per-cluster rates. Also must ensure we always keep the trace_id and job_id un-sampled. If sampling drops those, debugging is impossible. We should mark them as "always_keep": ["trace_id","job_id"].

olivia: Quick snippet for the parser to enforce non-droppable keys (jq):
```
if has("trace_id") | not then .trace_id = "<missing>" else . end
```
Also adding a light-weight sampling header in the ingest client: `x-rw-sampling: p=0.15,mode=per-request`

alex: We're also introducing a pii redaction hook. It's opt-in per-tenant for now; default behavior strips known PII fields (email, ssn, phone) using the redact pipeline stage. The redact stage outputs an audit token instead of raw data.

maria: Audit token is fine, but SOC asked for K-anonymity checks for some customer classes. Can we add a flag in the schema like `pii_level: "basic|k-anon|off"` so the pipeline can choose stricter heuristics?

alex: Yes — v2.1 includes `pii_level`. We will map: basic -> regex redaction, k-anon -> k=5 hashing+salt (salt stored in KMS). Off -> pass-through for internal-only tenants.

jun: Operational ask: when you flip sampling for a region, can the rollout be gradual? I want a step policy: 0.02 -> 0.05 -> 0.15 over 20m windows to avoid sudden bursts. Also tag rollouts with a run-id so we can correlate load spikes to config changes.

alex: Will do. Run-id will be `rw-roll-<ts>`. Rollouts go through canary pool first (dedicated capacity) then global.

ingest-bot: ingestion-config-service updated schema to v2.1 for cluster gpu-prod-1 at 1823456845 — status: rolling

sam: Action items:
- alex: push compatibility layer and schema docs (ETA: EOD today)
- olivia: add `x-rw-sampling` client header to SDKs + example (ETA: tomorrow)
- maria: adjust Grafana alert queries to stable keys and add schema version panel (ETA: 2d)
- jun: prepare region rollout policy and cost delta estimate for APAC (ETA: 2d)

maria: One more thing — let's create a short checklist for oncall before and after the flip (alert thresholds, low-cardinality dashboards, cost watch). I'll draft it and drop in #incidents. :thumbsup:

alex: Awesome — thanks everyone. I'll post links to the schema doc and the compatibility test run logs in this thread when available.
